Question: Let \(\mathsf H\subsetneq \mathsf G\) be compact connected semisimple Lie groups with \(\mathsf G/\mathsf H\) simply connected and almost effective. Let \(\mathsf A\) be a maximal torus in \(\N_{\mathsf G}(\mathsf H)/\mathsf H\), with \(\dim \mathsf A\ge 2\), and fix \(0<\ell<\dim \mathsf A\). For each \(i\in\mathbb N\), let \(\tilde A_i\subset \mathsf A\) be a compactly embedded subtorus of dimension \(\dim\mathsf A-\ell\), so that \(M_i^n=\mathsf G/\mathsf H\tilde A_i\) is a homogeneous \(\ell\)-torus bundle. Assume each \((\mathsf G/\mathsf H\tilde A_i,g_i)\) is a \(\mathsf G\)-homogeneous Einstein torus bundle of submersion type, meaning that any \(\mathsf G\)-invariant metric is also right \(\mathsf A\)-invariant, and that all metrics have Einstein constant \(1\). Convergence in the Grassmannian topology means convergence of the defining subtori \(\tilde A_i\) in the Grassmannian parameterizing such subtori. What is the strongest compactness statement that holds for such a sequence?
Predicted label: 'D'
Predicted text: 'After passing to a subsequence, \\((\\mathsf G/\\mathsf H\\tilde A_i,g_i)\\) converges in the Grassmannian topology to a limit \\((M_\\infty^n,g_\\infty)=(\\mathsf G/\\mathsf H\\tilde A_\\infty,g_\\infty)\\), where the limit is a (locally) \\(\\mathsf G\\)-homogeneous Einstein torus bundle.'
Correct label: 'D'
Correct text: 'After passing to a subsequence, \\((\\mathsf G/\\mathsf H\\tilde A_i,g_i)\\) converges in the Grassmannian topology to a limit \\((M_\\infty^n,g_\\infty)=(\\mathsf G/\\mathsf H\\tilde A_\\infty,g_\\infty)\\), where the limit is a (locally) \\(\\mathsf G\\)-homogeneous Einstein torus bundle.'
